lab.title: How alike the agents are, in every lab condition
lab.caption: Each dot is a world. Top: how many kinds of staking its agents fall into, counted by the agents in each (an effective number; logarithmic axis). Bottom: how far apart two agents' stakes are in the same situation and with the same random inputs, divided by how far apart two fresh founder brains are in the same situations: 1 means as different as brains drawn at random, less means more alike. Orange: B1 and its variants; blue: B2 and its variants; green: B2 with lapsing links. B2 without random inputs is left out of both: without noise every difference counts, and its kinds cannot be compared. B1: B1 at 10,000 tokens (Experiment 2); fixed: brains that never change (Experiment 7); B1 5k, B1 100k, B1 sizes: B1 at 5,000 (Experiment 12), 100,000 (Experiment 10) and 3,200 to 204,800 tokens (Experiment 8). B2: B2 at 10,000 tokens (Experiment 16); m .05 to m .8: the chance that a copied brain changes, 0.05 to 0.8 (B2's own is 0.2; Experiment 9); keep 1, keep ½: the last token kept, half the tokens kept; child: children of any size; no age: no old age (Experiment 15); B2 5k: B2 at 5,000 tokens, and with one of its rules taken away — no link: no links at birth, no val.: no valence, hand: handover allowed, no mend: no mending, lapse: any unused link lapses (Experiment 14).
lab.recipe:
**Runs.** Three seeds of every condition of the lab's experiments at the end of their runs (Experiments 7 to 16; B2 itself from Experiment 16 at 2,000 iterations and B1 from Experiment 2 at 3,000), and both seeds of every pilot condition at its checkpoint of 1,000 or 2,000 iterations.

**Data.** From `GraphOfLifeRuns/.pilots/diversity/across_lab.json`, `B1.json`, `B2.json` (`research/oee/checks/diversity.py`).

1. Load the world and play one game, so its messages are fresh (`research/oee/checks/diversity.py`).
2. Take what 200 living agents read, and draw their random input rows 8 times, the same draws for every brain.
3. Put the brains of 400 agents drawn at random, and 400 fresh founder brains, into every situation and draw, and turn their outputs into decisions by the engine's rules.
4. Count the kinds of staking as in [How different are the agents?](how-different-are-the-agents.md); divide the agents' total variation by the founders'.

**To make it again:** `python3 book_figures.py how_alike`.

pilots.title: Kinds of staking in the pilot worlds
pilots.caption: Each dot is a pilot world at its checkpoint of 1,000 iterations (batches A, N and S) or 2,000 (batches P and Q), the bar the median; orange: B1's rules underneath, blue: B2's. The pages that ran each batch say what its conditions change. Batch S: lottery, genotype, kin, family, fam. pool — contests by lottery, sides pooled by genotype, an eye for kin, an eye for a family tag, sides pooled by family (all without revolutions); B2, norev, gifts, g.+lapse, lapse, by tok. — B2 itself, without revolutions, with gifts, with gifts and every unused link lapsing, with every unused link lapsing, estates shared by wealth; B1, B1norev — B1, and B1 without revolutions.
